evidence.exact_text: 194. L'article L. 561-15-1 prévoit la communication systématique d'informations (COSI) à Tracfin relatives à des opérations identifiées comme présentant un risque élevé de blanchiment ou de financement du terrorisme en raison du pays ou du territoire d'origine ou de destination des fonds, de la nature des opérations en cause ou des structures juridiques impliquées dans ces opérations. notes.formalization: Paragraph 35 explicitly recommends applying CDD to customers, persons acting on their behalf and beneficial owners. recommendedTarget preserves should instead of asserting performed CDD or identifying a real person. The rule conjoins the two beyond-customer targets and introduces only the exact closed catalogue goal. It does not implement the separate identification/verification requirement or identify a beneficial owner from ownership/control facts.
notes.scope: BCBS is the non-national Basel guidance scope, not a claim that the recommendation is binding French or EU law. The one-day interval is an execution snapshot boundary. No exact legal effective date is inferred from the July 2020 edition. Notes 22–24 and paragraphs 36–38 were inspected as context.
notes.vocabulary: PersonsActingForCustomers denotes persons acting on customers behalf in the source, with representatives used only as an explanatory alias. BeneficialOwners remains a source-defined role; note 23 clarifies natural persons and alternative ownership/control/on-behalf limbs, without asserting that any real person meets them. notes.answer: The English answer preserves the recommendation and source scope, and explicitly declines to identify an owner or determine a national exemption. notes.location: PDF page 12 (printed page 8), paragraph 35, footnotes 22–24; adjacent paragraphs 36–38.

evidence.exact_text: 35. For the purposes of this guidance, a customer refers, in accordance with the FATF Recommendation 10, to any person 22 who enters into a business relationship or carries out an occasional financial transaction with the bank. The customer due diligence should be applied not only to customers but also to persons acting on their behalf and beneficial owners. 23 In accordance with the FATF standards, banks should identify customers and verify their identity. 24
22 "Person" in this context refers to natural and legal persons or legal arrangements.

23 The term "beneficial owner" is used in this guidance paper consistently with the definition and clarifications provided by the FATF standards. As a reminder, the FATF defines a "beneficial owner" as the natural person(s) who ultimately owns or controls a customer and/or natural person on whose behalf a transaction is being conducted. It also includes those persons who exercise ultimate effective control over a legal person or arrangement.
